chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his female slave to a man, should he separate them if he wishes? He said: If she is his slave, he may separate them if he wishes, for Allah, the Exalted, says: 'A slave who has no power over anything,' so the slave has no authority in the matter. And if her husband is free, then her divorce is her transaction (option). It is also possible that the meaning is if the master of the girl had stipulated for the husband at the time of the marriage contract that the divorce is in his hand, because that is permissible among the female slaves.
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to divorce a slave who is married to a free person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the legal nuances of 'tadbir' and marital authority, distinguishing between a slave husband whose master holds the right of divorce and a free husband who retains autonomy. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that a slave's legal capacity is often mediated by his master, particularly regarding the dissolution of marriage with a free woman. The text also notes the permissibility of stipulating the master's right to divorce as a condition in the marriage contract for female slaves.
